editorial.headline: Textile Packing, With a Clear National and Bali Position
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contract packing for textiles and textile products, from secure wrapping and labelling to sterilisation, and is open nationally to foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
Textile packing is often treated as a minor back-office function, yet this activity has a distinct commercial identity: providing packaging services for textile and textile products on a fee-for-service or contract basis. The work may be automated or manual. Its scope includes packing, secure wrapping, labelling, marking, product sterilisation and other related packing activity. In other words, the business is not defined by making the textiles, but by handling the process that prepares textile goods for onward movement or presentation.

The activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record recognises the same underlying activity across the full progression of enterprise sizes, rather than reserving it for a particular type of operator. A business registering this activity is therefore positioned around the service of packaging itself: the practical work of enclosing, securing, identifying, marking or sterilising textile products under an arrangement of remuneration or contract.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. At the national level, its PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no stated national ownership cap below full foreign ownership in this record. For founders considering a foreign-owned registration, that is the central national fact: the activity is open to PMA at the stated ceiling.

Bali adds a scale-sensitive reading, but not a prohibition. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record states that at the Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. It is therefore not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The applicable moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province; this activity is expressly recorded as outside that block because of its risk position at the Besar scale. For this textile-packing activity, the honest picture is consequently one of national foreign openness and a Bali position that remains available rather than barred, while recognising the higher-risk classification recorded at the large-business scale.
